data.name: Fabian
data.gender_notes: Fabian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Fabian is derived from the Latin word "fabius", which means "from Fabia". Fabia is the name of an ancient Roman clan. The name Fabian has been popular among Christians due to several figures in Christian history. It is also found in the Bible as the name of a Roman centurion who was healed by Jesus. The name Fabian carries the meaning “Man from Fabia” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Fabian usually hope their child will grow to embody man from fabia and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Fabian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man from Fabia.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fabian total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: פאביאן
in_hebrew.meaning: מקור - פאביוס, משמעות - חבר, חבר, קשור לאבן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור - פאביוס, פאביוס הוא שם שמשמעותו - חבר, חבר, קשור לאבן. בשפה העברית, פאביאן יכול להיות קואלקיונים, חבר, או קשור לאבן. בספרות הנוצרית, פאביאן היה פפיסט, שקשור לפפיסטים. השם פאביאן נפוץ בעיקר בקרב יהודים ונוצרים, ובמידה פחותה - בקרב אנשי דת אחרים. בשפה האנגלית, פאביאן הוא שם נפוץ, ובעיקר נודע בשל האישיות הפפיסטית, פאביאן.

in_greek.name: Φαβιανός
in_greek.meaning: πηγή - Φαβιανός, σημασία - φίλος, φίλος, συνδεδεμένος με πέτρα
in_greek.long_meaning: πηγή - Φαβιανός, Φαβιανός ήταν ονοματεπώνυμο που σημαίνει φίλος, φίλος, συνδεδεμένος με πέτρα. Στην αρχαία ελληνική γλώσσα, Φαβιανός ήταν συνώνυμο για φίλο ή φίλη. Στην Βίβλο, δεν υπάρχει καμία αναφορά για το ονοματεπώνυμο Φαβιανός. Ο Φαβιανός είναι γνωστός από την ομώνυμη εποχή της Ρωμαϊκής Αυτοκρατορίας, κατά την οποία ήταν ένα κοινό όνομα για τους χριστιανούς.

in_latin.name: Fabianus
in_latin.meaning: origo - Fabianus, significatio - amicus, amicus, coniunctus lapidi
in_latin.long_meaning: origo - Fabianus, Fabianus fuit nomen quod significat amicus, amicus, coniunctus lapidi. In lingua Latina, Fabianus fuit nomen commune, quod significat amicum vel amicam. In religione Christiana, Fabianus fuit nomen sacerdotum, qui erant coniuncti sibi et sibi invicem. Nomen Fabianus est originis Romanae, a quo nomen Fabii, familia nobilis Romana, derivatur.

It was common among the nobility, and many saints bear the name. European explorers and settlers brought the name to the New World, where it continues to be used. Today, Fabian is a multicultural name that is popular around the world, and it carries the legacy of its rich history and cultural associations.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Fabian is the name of several saints, including St. Fabian, who was the bishop of Rome from 236 to 249 AD. He is remembered for his bravery and unwavering commitment to the faith, even in the face of persecution. Fabian is also the name of a Christian martyr who was beheaded in Milan around 408 AD. These stories of courage and faith have inspired generations of Christians, and the name Fabian continues to be a reminder of the enduring qualities of perseverance and devotion. Additionally, the name Fabian is associated with the story of the Roman centurion who was healed by Jesus (Matthew 8:5-13). This story illustrates the power and compassion of Christ, and the name Fabian serves as a reminder of the spiritual healing and salvation that is available to all who seek it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Fabian derives from the Roman family name Fabius, meaning 'bean grower' or 'prosperous'. In Christian tradition, St. Fabian was the Pope during the persecution of Emperor Decius, known for his unwavering faith and martyrdom, symbolizing strength and resilience in the face of adversity.

historical_references.reference:
Saint Fabian was the bishop of Rome from 236 to 250 AD. He is considered a martyr, having been put to death during the persecutions of the Roman Emperor Decius.
Source: Catholic Encyclopedia.

Fabian, a Roman military commander, was consul in 274 AD during the reign of Emperor Aurelian. During his consulship, he played a key role in the defeat of the invading Goths at the Battle of Naissus.
Source: Ancient History List.
